newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips soar as tobacco talks ignite rally.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips soar as tobacco talks ignite rally.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks soared for the second consecutive day Wednesday, powered by news that tobacco companies were in talks with state attorneys general on a settlement of massive litigation against the industry.
The sharp gain extended into a third session the blue chips' bounce from last week's sell-off.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 92.71 points, or 1.41 percent, at 6,679.87.
With the gain, the Dow index has recovered 288 points, or more than 40 percent, of the nearly 700-point plunge between March 11 and April 11.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,401 to 1,038 on active volume of 499 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The news that tobacco companies were negotiating to settle the long-running lawsuits sparked new life into tobacco shares and helped stocks advance despite a weak performance by bonds.
Philip Morris Cos. led the rally, jumping 4-1/4 to 43-1/4. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. was up 3-1/4 at 33-1/2. Loews Corp., which owns Lorillard Tobacco Co., was 5-3/8 higher at 91-3/4.

"We got off to a good start with the positive reaction to the potential tobacco settlement," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management. "This was the first time in awhile that bonds were a touch soft and stocks were more than a touch strong," he said.
But even as blue chips were roaring ahead, many analysts focused on the broad market, which was fairly mixed.
Once again, technology shares failed to take part in the rally, resulting in a second consecutive decline for the Nasdaq Composite index, which ended 2.61 points lower at 1,210.27.
Also weaker were interest-rate sensitive groups such as banks, which met with early selling pressure after new data showed economic activity continues at a bustling pace.
The data included industrial output and manufacturing capacity utilization.
"This is not the kind of scenario from which bulls are born," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp.
The 30-year Treasury bond was off 1/32, sending its yield up to 7.10 percent from Tuesday's close of 7.09 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
Among financial stocks, Chase Manhattan Corp. fell 2-7/8 to 89-3/4 and Citicorp lost 2-1/2 to 104-3/8.
Analysts said the interest rate environment meant that the outlook for the group and the broad market remained cloudy, despite the recent blue-chip bounce.
"Stocks are still not inherently cheap, and after earnings are through, people will start focusing on (Federal Reserve Chairman) Mr. Greenspan again and that's not going to bring joy," Stein said.
For now, however, earnings hold centre stage, and the session saw several issues roar to solid advances after stronger-than-expected profits.
Among companies whose results beat Wall Street estimates were Colgate-Palmolive Co., which rose 2-3/8 to 107-1/8, and Ford Motor Co., up 1-1/2 to 34-3/4.
In contrast, investors punished companies where there was a hint of slower profit or revenue growth.
Clarify Inc. plunged 9-3/4 to seven after the help-desk software developer said it expects little, if any revenue growth in the second quarter.
The dim outlook drove down other stocks in Clarify's market niche. Remedy Corp. tumbled 7-3/4 to 32-11/16 and Scopus Technology Inc. slid 5-1/4 to 22-7/8.
National Education Corp. rose 4-3/8 to 19-3/8 after publishing company Harcourt General Inc. launched a $19.50 per share cash tender offer for the company.
Harcourt said the offer represented a 15 percent premium over National Education's proposed stock merger with Sylvan Learning Systems Inc., announced last month.
Sylvan Learning rose one point to 30-1/8 and Harcourt jumped 2-1/8 to 45.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 8.81 points to 763.53. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.45 to 556.51.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 4.13 to 401.75. The average share was up 41 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,242.99, up 57.489 or 0.80 percent.
